name: Lmc Industries Inc
old_description: Since 1945, we’ve been working with OEMs and tiered suppliers to drive part design innovation that moves businesses forward. In fact, LMC engineering is behind many modern conveniences such as the press-down valve on whipped topping cans!
about:
LMC Industries operates from Arnold, Missouri, where it was founded in 1945 by toolmaker Fred Suellentrop Sr. The company remains family-owned and traces its start to Suellentrop's goal of building high-quality equipment that improves the manufacturability of essential products.

The company provides precision metal stamping — including progressive die stamping, in-die tapping, and in-die assembly — alongside plastic injection molding, insert molding, and overmolding. It also runs a 14,000-square-foot tool room equipped with CNC milling, wire and conventional EDM, water jet machining, and TIG welding for in-house die and mold fabrication, repair, and maintenance. All operations share a 240,000-square-foot facility housing more than 80 stamping and injection molding presses.

LMC serves OEMs and tiered suppliers in automotive, agricultural, consumer products, medical device, and hand-tool markets. Automotive customers include every major global automaker; agricultural programs cover harvesting equipment and livestock feeding systems; consumer products range from screwdriver and toothbrush handles to medical device grips and automotive interior touchpoints.

The company emphasizes a single-source model for metal and plastic components, which it says simplifies purchasing, compresses lead times, and creates a single point of quality accountability. Its differentiators include Design for Manufacturability applied to every program, a transfer-tooling process for taking over existing programs, PPAP and APQP quality systems with first-article inspection, and a dedicated team focused on proactive communication.

name: Locust Grove Woodworks
old_description: I have been building fine quality furniture and wood products since 1982. I have had an unusual journey, having been a part of the Amish and related Mennonite groups for most of my life. Their legendary ascetical worldviews had a profound influence on my work and manner of construction.
about:
Locust Grove Woodworks operates from Thorndike, Maine, where it was founded in 1982 by a craftsman who spent much of his life in Amish and Mennonite communities. The founder's background in those ascetical traditions shaped a philosophy of simplicity, durability, and sustainable production that still guides the shop today.

The one-person workshop produces heirloom-grade solid-wood furniture piece by piece, using a mix of hand tools and power equipment driven partly by draft horses. Construction relies on traditional joinery such as sliding dovetails and floating tenons to accommodate wood movement, and finishes are hand-applied linseed oil and wax. The catalog spans beds, chairs, tables, desks, clocks, cradles, coffins, and custom casework.

Each item is built to order, with no inventory of mass-produced stock.

The business was started to create furniture that could be passed down for generations, inspired by the Shaker maxim to build as if you were to live a thousand years but die tomorrow. The founder's commitment to low-impact, horse-powered manufacturing remains a defining characteristic.

name: Loeb Electric
old_description: With four central Ohio electrical supply stores, we proudly serve the local contractor market. Nationally, we partner with the world’s most recognized brands to build, improve, and maintain their stores.
about:
Loeb Electric is headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, with four retail stores in central Ohio (including Hilliard). Founded in 1912 in Columbus by Oscar Avery and Arthur Loeb Sr. as The Avery & Loeb Electric Company, the business paused briefly during the Great Depression before Arthur Loeb restarted it. Ownership has passed through three generations of the Loeb family and remains family‑owned today, led by President Charles Loeb.

The company operates as an independent electrical distributor with four distribution centers, 400,000+ sq. ft. of warehouse space, 35+ delivery trucks, and 350+ team members. It stocks electrical distribution & controls, lighting fixtures & bulbs, wire & conduit, and tools. Value‑added services include vendor‑managed inventory (VMI) with consigned stock options, project material management, wire cutting/harnessing/parallel/coiling and pulling‑head installation, supply kitting, 24/7 locker pickup (Loeb Lockers), same‑day delivery, and after‑hours emergency service. The facility processes over 500 orders — comprising 8,000+ line items — daily.

Loeb serves two primary customer groups: local electrical contractors in central Ohio and national multi‑site brands (retail, commercial) across the United States. Its national accounts division provides preventative and reactive maintenance services for brands with multiple locations, while contractor‑focused solutions such as VMI, kitting, and wire services aim to increase jobsite productivity.

The company emphasizes trust, personal service, and commitment to customer success, as stated by President Charles Loeb. It differentiates through its "Loeb Difference" — combining local presence with national reach, continuous improvement, and innovative programs in sustainable lighting, jobsite productivity, and wire services.

about:
Lotel was founded in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, in 1964 by John L. Lowery. Shortly after establishing the company, Lowery invented and patented the Mesh-Up® line of plastic chairs used to support welded wire mesh in concrete slabs. The business has remained in Baton Rouge, where it continues to produce its patented products and offer custom molding services.

The company manufactures Mesh-Ups® and Rebar-Ups®, which are globally patented supports for concrete reinforcement. Production takes place on five injection molding machines at its Baton Rouge facility.

Lowery’s original invention was recognized as the first practical flexible chair for welded wire mesh, earning patents in over 50 countries. The current product line holds multiple U.S. patents (including Nos. 6,962,029; 7,458,192; and D491,443) and registered trademarks worldwide. The company emphasizes engineering superiority, increased stability, ease of use, and competitive pricing for contractors.

name: Louisa Food Products, Inc
old_description: Our mission is to be recognized as the leading provider of high-quality, frozen, filled pasta. To achieve this mission, Louisa Foods stays true to the core values that launched our success from the start.
about:
Louisa Food Products, Inc. operates from St. Louis, Missouri. The company traces its roots back over 50 years when St. Louis restaurateur Ferdinando Baldetti began producing scratch-made ravioli and pasta for local restaurants. Today, the business remains family-owned, now spanning four generations of the Baldetti family.

The company specializes in frozen, filled pasta products including toasted ravioli, ravioli, and tortellini. Production follows a daily scratch-kitchen approach: doughs are mixed from carefully milled wheat, vegetables are hand-chopped and roasted, meats are braised and stocks reduced in-house, cheeses are freshly grated, and pasta is made with semolina flour and eggs. The facility houses a culinary center for ongoing recipe development.

Louisa Foods serves both foodservice and retail channels.

The Baldetti family's founding belief that "freshness matters" continues to drive operations. The company states its mission is to be recognized as the provider of high-quality frozen filled pasta, built on honesty, integrity, and responsiveness to customer needs.

about:
Lumen Food Labs LLC, operating under the Lumen Brands name, is headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. The company was founded in 2020.

The firm provides master distributor and compliance services for consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands seeking to enter the U.S. market. Its offerings include Foreign Supplier Verification Program (FSVP) and Qualified Importer (QI) management, FDA-certified third-party logistics (3PL) warehousing, and acting as importer of record, customs broker, clearing house, insurer, and FDA responsible party. Lumen purchases inventory upfront at wholesale prices and provides monthly accounting, sales reporting, and forecasting from its Chicago warehouse facility.

Brand partners engage the company to handle facility registration, product identification, and all shipment-level compliance obligations for goods entering the United States.

The company differentiates itself by committing to purchase products upfront with no contingency, matching brand partners' investments dollar-for-dollar, and tying its own profitability directly to the successful sale of those products. This model is designed to align incentives and reduce risk for brands expanding into the U.S. market.

name: M-Tron Components Inc
old_description: Since 1984, M-TRON Components has maintained a commitment to excellence and has provided our customers with a secure supply chain
about:
M-Tron Components Inc. was founded in 1984 in Ronkonkoma, New York. The company operates as a veteran-owned small business and a franchised distributor of electronic components, emphasizing a secure supply chain for military and commercial customers.

The firm stocks a broad inventory of semiconductors, resistors, capacitors, interconnect devices, and computer products from authorized manufacturers. Value-added services include mil-spec packaging per MIL-STD-2073, barcoding and RFID tagging to MIL-STD-129, kitting, tape-and-reel, printed circuit board assembly, and a proprietary search-and-sell network for obsolete or allocated parts. Quality management is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9120:2016, the latter addressing aerospace chain-of-custody and anti-counterfeit controls.

Primary customers are the U.S. Government, its subcontractors, and OEMs in the military and aerospace sectors. M-Tron is a certified NDAA (H.R. 1540) supplier and participates in Lockheed Martin’s Star Supplier Program. about:
Mace MFG is based in Indian Land, South Carolina. Founded in 2023 by Stuart, a mechanical engineer, the company began as a nights-and-weekends project using 3D printers and CNC routers. After fabricating a replacement floor for a 1974 Toyota Land Cruiser with a CNC plasma table, Stuart sold a 1993 Nissan Skyline GT-R in February 2023 to purchase a HAAS VF2 vertical machining center, committing full-time to producing machined automotive accessories.

The shop focuses on precision-machined accessories for off-road Toyota and Lexus vehicles. Using the HAAS VF2 alongside 3D printing and CNC plasma cutting, Mace MFG produces billet aluminum volume knobs (marketed as "Knobbies"), titanium-and-Ultem key fob cases, battery tie-downs, shift knobs, front bump stops, rail T-nuts, and battery clamp J-hooks. Materials include 6061 aluminum, titanium, Ultem (PEI), and polycarbonate. The product line spans multiple SKUs across 4Runner, Tundra, Tacoma, Sequoia, GX, LX, and FJ Cruiser models.

The company serves the automotive aftermarket, specifically off-road and overlanding enthusiasts driving Toyota and Lexus trucks and SUVs. Customers purchase directly through the Mace MFG web store; notable community figures such as Keith Charvonia of Charvonia Design, Patrick Perry of Perry Parts, and Colten Johnson of Teton Workshop are featured as collaborators.

Mace MFG emphasizes American manufacturing and engineering-driven design, stating that every detail is scrutinized to deliver quality without compromise. The founder's background in automotive design and manufacturing informs a philosophy of "innovation drives us" and "from our hands to yours."

name: Machined In Wood
old_description: Machined In Wood is a custom CNC woodworking shop that specializes in CNC machined wood projects, laser engraving, and finishing of custom one of a kind pieces, prototypes, and small to medium scale manufacturing.
about:
Machined In Wood operates from Bellingham, Massachusetts. The shop began as a home-based business and has expanded to serve both individual clients and commercial manufacturers.

The company provides custom CNC woodworking services including V-carving, 3D carving, precision machined parts, and profile cuts in sheet goods. It also offers laser cutting and engraving with CO2 and diode lasers, 3D printing for prototyping, traditional woodworking (table saw, band saw, jointer, planer, drum sander, router, sanding), and painting and finishing such as hand painting, airbrushing, HVLP spraying, stains, clear coats, and food-grade finishes. Two 48" x 48" CNC routers (one with pass-through capability) and a horizontal boring machine support production runs from dozens to hundreds of parts.

Customers range from individual hobbyists and makers to other wood shops and commercial firms. The shop works with engineers and designers on production parts, accepting customer-supplied material and collaborating via blueprints, CAD models, and GD&T specifications. Projects include one-of-a-kind pieces, prototypes, and small-to-medium scale manufacturing for clients across the United States.

Machined In Wood differentiates itself with equipment that many small shops do not invest in, notably a horizontal boring machine for precise horizontal holes and the ability to flatten material up to 48" x 48" on its CNC routers. The company emphasizes proficiency with technical drawings and GD&T, maintains a 1% tolerance level, and conducts rigorous QA inspections. It also takes on smaller projects that larger shops often decline.

old_description: Mack Molding specializes in custom injection molding, providing high-quality plastic components tailored to diverse industry needs.
about:
Mack Molding Co. was founded in 1920 and operates as a vertically integrated contract manufacturer headquartered in Arlington, Vermont, with a southern division in Inman, South Carolina. The company began as a custom injection molding specialist and has expanded over more than a century into a multi-facility operation.

Today Mack Molding provides end-to-end manufacturing services including plastic injection molding (120+ presses ranging from 28 to 4,000 tons, shot sizes of 0.6 to 769 ounces), large-part molding, Class A painting, CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, assembly, and supply chain management. The company runs ten facilities totaling more than 1.5 million square feet of manufacturing space and supports production volumes from prototype quantities of five pieces up to five million units annually.

Its customer base spans medical device, industrial equipment, transportation, robotics, energy and utilities, and defense sectors, serving both publicly traded Fortune 500 companies and private enterprises. The firm is FDA and ITAR registered, enabling work on regulated medical products and defense programs.

Mack Molding emphasizes a “one partner, total responsibility” model, positioning itself as an extension of the client’s manufacturing team. It highlights financial stability (debt‑free with a 5A1 Dun & Bradstreet rating), deep in‑house engineering and tooling capabilities, and a vertically integrated approach designed to reduce lead times, coordinate multi‑material production, and maintain consistent quality across complex programs.

old_description: In business since 1975, Macy is made up of a hardworking team of knowledgeable metal fabrication experts with quality and integrity in mind. From our family to yours, we appreciate your support and look forward to accommodating your metal fabrication needs.
about:
Macy Industries operates from Hooksett, New Hampshire, where it has been providing custom metal fabrication since 1975.

The shop delivers design, fabrication, installation, and maintenance services across a range of metal products. Its capabilities span custom dust and fume collection systems, industrial ventilation, stainless steel tanks, medical laboratory and commercial kitchen countertops, mezzanines, handrails, exhaust hoods, grease ducts, stairs, railings, exhaust stacks, power-lift doors, and spiral ductwork. The team works with stainless steel, aluminum, galvanized metal, copper, and carbon fiber, producing everything from architectural features such as copper hoods and retractable roofs to structural frames, machine guarding, and platforms.

Customers come from commercial, industrial, and residential sectors. Construction managers, general contractors, builders, and architects rely on Macy for metal staircases, railings, balconies, awnings, and hydraulic doors. Facility managers and industrial engineers specify its dust, fume, and mist collection systems, while homeowners and residential architects commission copper gutters, countertops, and custom railings. The company also serves architectural millwork shops, plumbing and HVAC contractors, and restaurant and hotel projects.

Macy emphasizes a collaborative process that integrates engineering design, production, and installation under one roof, a model it says keeps clients returning with new projects. The firm highlights its engineering talent and flexibility to produce difficult-to-replicate products as its competitive advantage.

old_description: I have been very happy with the three 15kva transformers we purchased from Maddox. The team is ready to please, friendly and actually helpful. The cost vs quality is unfounded. about:
Maddox Industrial Transformer is headquartered in Battle Ground, Washington, with additional facilities in Greer and Simpsonville, South Carolina; Fountain Inn, South Carolina; Batavia, Ohio; Moscow, Idaho; Houston, Texas; and Woodruff, South Carolina. The company was founded in 2015 by Camden Spiller and a team of transformer industry veterans whose experience dates back to the 1980s. It remains privately owned and has grown to employ more than 400 people across its seven U.S. locations.

The company designs, manufactures, and warrants padmount, substation, polemount, and dry-type transformers ranging from 3 kVA to 160,000 kVA, along with pad-mounted and metal-enclosed switchgear up to 35 kV. It also operates a national service network providing transformer repair, rewinding, and maintenance; a rental fleet of low- and medium-voltage units; a surplus purchasing program; and a parts inventory covering fluid, bushings, fuses, and gauges. Maddox reports having shipped over 100,000 transformers and maintains thousands of units in stock for same-day dispatch.

Customers span data centers, manufacturers, renewable energy developers, electrical distributors, bitcoin mining operations, electrical contractors, and real estate developers. The firm emphasizes commercial and industrial projects rather than utility accounts, citing clients such as a lumber mill, an irrigation district, a data center operator, and an electric bus fleet.

Maddox positions itself on speed and purchasing simplicity—offering quotes within 30 minutes, same-day shipping on stock units, and expedited production slots for custom builds—while still meeting ANSI, NEMA, DOE, and IEEE standards. Leadership says the company was started to give commercial and industrial buyers the lead times and responsiveness typically reserved for utility customers.

name: Majestic Metals by Fathom Manufacturing
old_description: Majestic Metals was founded in 1979. Across more than 45 years, the company has built an exceptional reputation for service, quality, and speed in sheet metal fabrication.
about:
Majestic Metals by Fathom Manufacturing operates a sheet metal fabrication facility in Denver, Colorado. The business was founded in 1979 as Majestic Metals and has accumulated more than 45 years of experience in precision fabrication. Today it operates as part of the Fathom Manufacturing network, maintaining the same end-to-end approach that defined its early years.

The Denver facility takes parts from cutting and forming through finishing and final assembly, delivering complete fabricated products rather than loose components. Core processes include laser cutting (fiber, solid-state, and CO2), CNC punching, press-brake forming up to 12 feet and 220 tons, welding (arc, MIG, TIG, spot, and laser), captive hardware installation, painting, powder coating, screen printing, mechanical and electro-mechanical assembly, and in-house CNC machining for post-mill features. The shop runs three fiber/solid-state lasers, two CO2 lasers, five punch presses, thirteen press brakes, twelve TIG welders, seven MIG welders, and one laser welder, with automated loading that enables lights-out production for runs of 100 to 10,000 pieces. Work spans prototype through full production across aluminum, steel, and stainless steel from 0.010 to 0.50 inch thick, holding ±0.005 inch on cutting and punching.

The facility serves data-center and IT infrastructure, EV charging equipment, medical device housings, self-service kiosks and retail technology, industrial equipment enclosures, military and defense, automotive, energy, agriculture, semiconductor, and consumer electronics and lighting. Customers include a major semiconductor manufacturer that cites accuracy, flatness, and consistency across runs.

The company emphasizes a single-source model that eliminates multi-vendor coordination, a value-engineering mindset applied from prototype to production, design-for-manufacturability support, and a 98% on-time delivery rate. ITAR registration allows it to handle government and defense projects.

about:
Manchester Packaging Company was founded in 1969 in St. James, Missouri. The company began with the goal of providing customers with quality economical packaging, a tradition it continues today.

The company operates as a custom manufacturer of polyethylene blown film and bags. Its core processes include mono-layer and three-layer co-extrusion using prime resins, producing films with no-slip, medium-slip, high-slip, linear clarity, and biopolymer blends. Flexographic printing capability covers one to eight colors in line or process designs, with both surface and reverse printing on film and bags. Bag manufacturing includes printed and unprinted side-seal and bottom-seal configurations made to custom sizes within equipment limits. The facility also offers U.S. Postal Service mail overwrap services.

Manchester Packaging serves manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, and retail businesses across the packaging sector. Its film and bag products are used in shrink film, form-fill-seal applications, wicketed bags, perforated-on-roll bags, and draw-tape bags.

The company emphasizes its FDA-approved polyethylene film and a waste-reduction practice that recycles and reprocesses 99 percent of production scrap. Its founding principle of delivering economical quality remains the stated differentiator.

about:
Manufacture Alabama operates from Montgomery as the state's sole trade association focused exclusively on the legislative, regulatory, and operational concerns of manufacturers and their partner businesses. The organization represents hundreds of companies ranging from global corporations to small family-owned operations, each described as a vital component of Alabama's economy and job base. No founding year or founder names are publicly disclosed.

The association provides a suite of services designed to support vibrant manufacturing operations, including environmental, safety, and human resources compliance assistance; government and regulatory representation; workforce development strategies; transportation and infrastructure initiatives; industry promotion; and tax, energy, and other policy support. A staff of five leads these efforts, headed by President & CEO Jon Barganier, alongside specialists in government affairs, workforce development, communications, and an affiliated executive director role.

Membership is divided into two categories: Manufacturing Members and Partner Members. Programs such as Girls Learning About Manufacturing (GLAM) aim to cultivate future talent by creating interest in manufacturing careers among female students entering the workforce.

Manufacture Alabama states its mission as creating a business and political climate that promotes a positive, competitive environment and enhances growth opportunities for Alabama manufacturers.

name: Maple Lane Farms LLC
old_description: A 5-generation family farm with a colorful and wholesome history. Our story is one of determination and never giving up. Farming has never been easy, and so to keep up the good fight we’ve diversified. We offer hay, feed sales, and custom processing for your beef & pork. We now have a retail store as well as currently selling locally raised beef, pork, and chicken. You order in a call-in manner, we fill it for you and call you when it’s ready. To our current customers, thank you for choosing us, and to our new visitors, welcome, and we hope to become friends soon. As always, cash, check, credit, debit, and EBT are accepted.
about:
Maple Lane Farms operates from Charleston, Maine, on a property first purchased by Stanley Higgins in 1935. The farm passed to Charles “Shine” and Margaret Higgins in 1941 and evolved from a potato, dairy, and hay operation into a multi-generation family business. In 1999, Barry and Mary Higgins acquired the farm from Charles and established the current Maple Lane Farms entity, continuing a lineage that now spans five generations.

The farm raises approximately 700 head of cattle and processes its own beef, pork, and chicken in a state-inspected facility expanded in 2005 and again in 2011 to add refrigeration and an automated smokehouse. Operations include custom slaughter and cutting for outside livestock, hay and silage production (round and square bales stored indoors), and screened compost made from processing waste, cow manure, and horse barn waste. A retail store sells flash-frozen cuts, sausages, bacon, and the farm’s “Black Label Reserve” beef, with orders filled Monday through Friday.

Customers include local households buying retail meat, farmers needing custom processing for their own animals, horse owners purchasing horse-quality hay, and gardeners using the farm’s compost. The farm also supplies feed and serves as one of the largest hay dealers in the Northeast, selling silage by the ton and hay by the bale.

The Higgins family emphasizes hands-on work—every cut, sausage link, and label is done by hand—and the farm’s diversification was driven by the need to sustain the operation through changing regulations and market pressures.

about:
Mar-Med was founded in 1989 in Grand Rapids, Michigan, by Dr. Joseph Marogil, a general surgeon who invented the Tourni-Cot digital tourniquet to address a need he encountered in hand surgery. The company remains physician-founded and family-owned, operating from its original location near the city’s Medical Mile.

Today Mar-Med operates as an FDA-registered medical device manufacturing site certified to ISO 13485:2016. It designs and produces a line of disposable devices including the Tourni-Cot and Uni-Cot digit tourniquets, the Rhino-Pak epistaxis balloon, the Balloon Extractor for nasal foreign-body removal, the Derma-Stent abscess drain, and the ZEROWET wound-irrigation system. The company also handles global distribution of these products to healthcare facilities worldwide.

Mar-Med’s devices are used in emergency medicine, podiatry, pediatrics, and orthopedic surgery, serving hospitals, clinics, and other healthcare providers across the United States and internationally. The company emphasizes simple, cost-effective tools that support efficient procedures and positive patient outcomes.

The firm cites its family-owned structure, physician-led design perspective, and compliance with FDA QSR, ISO 13485, and European CE marking requirements as key differentiators. It also highlights sustainability practices such as composting label backing, recycling eligible waste, and reusing packaging materials.

about:
Marlin Steel, headquartered in Baltimore, Maryland, was established in 1968. The company began as a producer of bagel baskets before pivoting to custom-engineered wire and sheet metal products. The company manufactures material handling baskets, wire forms, and mobile carts using processes that include wire forming (0.003–0.625 inch diameter), sheet metal fabrication (up to 3 inches thick), steel machining, fixturing, welding, and a range of over 40 finishes such as electropolishing, Teflon, nylon, Halar, powder coating, and plastic coating. Marlin Steel serves aerospace, defense, medical, food processing, automotive, data center, and telecommunications industries. Examples include stainless steel carts and baskets for medical and pharmaceutical use, telecom equipment enclosures, aerospace engine floats and turbine blade carriers, food processing baskets meeting FDA requirements, and automotive wire baskets designed to reduce scrap and improve production tolerances.

The company emphasizes advanced automation and precision engineering as key differentiators, enabling custom design and quick turnaround. Its culture focuses on employee well-being and community investment, with leadership stating a commitment to treating workers well and strengthening the rural communities where its plants operate.

about:
Maryland Packaging, a food co-packaging and co-manufacturing company, was established in 2003 in Halethorpe, Maryland. The business operates two facilities in the state, including a location in Elkridge.

The company provides a full range of food production services: co-packaging, co-manufacturing, private labeling, fulfillment and logistics, high pressure processing (HPP), and tolling. Its HPP capacity—powered by two Hiperbaric 525 machines and one Avure 10—is described as the largest in the Mid-Atlantic, able to process over 3,000 kilograms per hour. A commercial kitchen incubator and accelerator supports product development, while packaging lines handle skin packaging, modified atmosphere packaging, bottling, sachets, and wet and dry packing. Maryland Packaging serves food and beverage businesses of all sizes, from start-ups to large enterprises. Clients include Sunniva Caffe and Mason Jar Cookie Company, both cited in testimonials. The company private-labels condiments, marinara and dipping sauces, dessert sauces, gazpacho soups, and smoothies, and co-packs products such as juices, smoothies, tea, coffee, ready-to-eat meals, spices, cookies, crackers, cheeses, and dairy items.

The company’s stated philosophy is “Under Promise, Over Deliver,” emphasizing transparency, honesty, and owning mistakes. It differentiates itself through its SQF-certified facility with one of the highest ratings in the United States, the ability to help brands achieve Organic, Kosher, Halal, and Non-GMO certifications, and a single-roof model that combines manufacturing, processing, packaging, R&D, lab testing, compliance, storage, and private labeling.

The company's stated mission is to help injection, extrusion, blow molding, and 3D printing operations become more profitable through better plasticating components and entirely new technologies. Its differentiation rests on patented innovations, proprietary analytical software, and a focus on custom engineering for specific resin and process requirements.

name: Meiden America Switchgear, Inc.
old_description: Meidensha Corporation has been providing employees with hands-on safety education designed to stimulate danger sensitivity since 2008. In December 2016, Meidensha Corporation also began selling on-site education for clients seeking it at plants, construction sites and other locations outside the Company. Hands-on safety education is more effective than other methods, and is helping eradicate workplace accidents. Lessons that simulate the experience of workplace accidents are provided in all-weather hands-on safety education vehicles that eliminate the need for student movement.
about:
Meiden America Switchgear, Inc. (MAS) was founded in 2020 and is headquartered in Gray Court, South Carolina, near Greenville. The company operates as a subsidiary of Meidensha Corporation, a Japanese manufacturer founded in 1897 in Tokyo. MAS was established to serve the North American power grid with high-voltage vacuum circuit breakers (VCBs) and vacuum interrupters (VIs), drawing on its parent company’s 125-year history in the industry. President Yukihiro Takeshita leads the operation, which celebrated its grand opening and first shipment on February 9, 2021.

MAS designs, manufactures, tests, and sells 72.5 kV and 145 kV dry-air insulated dead-tank vacuum circuit breakers, as well as vacuum interrupter bottles. Meidensha pioneered vacuum interrupter technology in the mid-1960s and produced the world’s first 72.5 kV dry-air VCB in 2002, delivering more than 2,500 units globally, including over 1,000 to North American customers. The 145 kV dry-air VCB, introduced in late 2021, was another world first. The Gray Court facility handles full production from design through testing.

The company serves electric power utilities across North America that are seeking to replace sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) gas with environmentally friendly dry-air insulation. It also supplies vacuum interrupters to North American original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) for integration into their own switchgear. The database lists power and energy and automotive testing systems as served industries.

MAS positions its dry-air VCBs as a green alternative that eliminates SF6, a potent greenhouse gas, while offering zero emissions and low maintenance. The company’s mission is to lead the industry by providing high-value products that integrate cutting-edge technology and help customers meet environmental challenges.

about:
Melanzana Outdoor Clothing was founded in 1994 in Leadville, Colorado, as a local manufacturer of outdoor apparel. The company remains rooted in Leadville, where it began with a commitment to keep production domestic rather than outsourcing overseas. Ownership has transitioned to an employee-owned model, with more than 20 workers holding stock and a long-term goal of full employee ownership.

The company designs, cuts, and sews a range of outdoor garments—including hoodies, base layers, and accessories—at its Leadville factory and a newer facility in Alamosa. Together the two sites employ over 80 people in Leadville and 40 in Alamosa. Melanzana has developed more than 50 original product designs and emphasizes U.S.-made fabrics, though it sources Merino wool from Thailand when domestic equivalents are unavailable.

Melanzana sells directly to consumers through its Leadville retail store and online shop, serving outdoor enthusiasts and mountain communities. The brand has become a fixture in the outdoor industry, with its hoodie design language widely imitated. The company also supports local nonprofits through programs such as PB & Melly, which offers paid employee time for community work, and 1% For The Outdoors, a voluntary donation program funding conservation and recreation groups in the region.

Founded on the principle of local manufacturing, Melanzana differentiates itself through employee ownership, a focus on high-quality domestic textiles, and deep community investment. The company states that its evolution—from a single Leadville shop to a two-town operation—reflects a desire to maintain quality while reducing customer wait times.

about:
Mercury Wire Products Inc. has operated from Spencer, Massachusetts since its founding in 1967. The company began as a custom wire and cable manufacturer and has remained independently owned, serving customers across the United States and internationally from its single Massachusetts facility.

The company designs and manufactures engineered wire, cable, and complete cable assemblies under one roof. Its capabilities span custom cable construction — selecting conductors, shielding, jacketing, and geometry for specific applications — through full assembly services that include crimping, connector termination, and testing. Leadership emphasizes a people-first, continuous-improvement culture built around what it calls its True North principles. The stated differentiator is the value-stream ownership structure, which eliminates handoffs between engineering, production, and logistics to accelerate decisions and reduce lead times. The DIVE process — Discover, Design & Prototype, Build & Scale, Deliver & Support — formalizes this end-to-end accountability.

about:
Methode Electronics was founded in 1946 by William J. McGinley on the south side of Chicago, Illinois. The company's name derived from an anagram of "good manufacturing method, electrode and cathode of a vacuum tube." McGinley, a World War II veteran, started the business with a focus on innovation and cutting-edge technology to engineer solutions for customers.

Today headquartered in Southfield, Michigan, Methode Electronics (NYSE: MEI) operates as a global manufacturer of custom-engineered mechatronic products. The company employs approximately 6,500 people across sales, engineering, and manufacturing locations in North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. Its vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities span assembly, decorating, electronics, metalworking, plastics, and testing, including processes such as injection molding, stamping, PCB assembly, in-mold decorating, and automated optical inspection. The business is organized into three segments—Automotive, Industrial, and Interface—each delivering highly integrated solutions for user interface, LED lighting, power distribution, and sensor applications.

Methode serves original equipment manufacturers across transportation, industrial, and consumer markets. Its automotive segment supplies user-interface, lighting, sensor, and chassis/powertrain solutions to automotive, commercial vehicle, bus, rail, and off-road OEMs. The Industrial segment, through brands such as Grakon, Nordic Lights, Power Solutions Group, and Hetronic, addresses markets including mining, material handling, agriculture, construction, military/aerospace, data centers, energy storage, robotics, and renewable energy. The Interface segment, via TouchSensor and Methode Sensor Technologies, provides touch, display, and sensor solutions for appliances, vending machines, medical equipment, fitness equipment, and e-mobility applications.

The company states its differentiation lies in proprietary and differentiated technology, expertise across multiple applications, highly vertically integrated manufacturing, quality and reliability, and responsiveness to global OEM customer needs. Founder William McGinley's original vision was to engineer and manufacture solutions that help customers grow their own businesses through innovation.

MiDAS Foods International operates from its main campus in Oak Park, Michigan, with a second facility in Birmingham, Alabama. The company has been developing dry blends and food solutions for over 40 years. Partners Richard Elias and Gary Freeman lead the business alongside a team of culinary and R&D executives.

about:
MicroLink Devices was founded in 2000 in Niles, Illinois, a northern suburb of Chicago. The company operates a 30,000-square-foot facility that houses a clean room, device fabrication and test laboratories, and a full suite of metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) tools for high-volume epitaxial growth.

The company designs and manufactures III-V epitaxial materials for wireless communications, including cellular phones, and produces high-efficiency single- and multi-junction gallium arsenide (GaAs) solar cells and sheets for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), spacecraft, and terrestrial collectors. Its proprietary epitaxial lift-off (ELO) process separates the solar cell structure from the growth substrate, yielding lightweight, flexible cells while allowing the substrate to be reused multiple times. MicroLink owns all equipment needed for growth, fabrication, and testing of epitaxial materials and solar devices.

Since 2003 it has been a prime federal contractor on more than thirty programs developing solar cells, transistors, and lasers. Its customer base includes government agencies and commercial firms seeking custom epitaxial materials, solar sheets for UAVs and satellites, and contract research and development support.

The company emphasizes quality and technical depth: it is ISO 9001 certified, employs staff recognized as experts in GaAs- and InP-based device growth and processing, and supports customers through both development and production phases to improve yield and performance. The ELO technology, developed through its federal R&D programs, is cited as a key differentiator that reduces cost and enables flexible, high-specific-power solar solutions.

The company emphasizes relationship‑driven service, welcoming complex projects and tight deadlines. Its employee‑ownership model and long‑standing community involvement are cited as foundations for consistent, cost‑effective delivery.

Mid State Welding LLC operates from Spearfish, South Dakota, where it was founded in 2020 by Rodney and Brooke Ross. The husband‑and‑wife team started the business after Rodney spent 13 years welding pipelines across the country and they saw a local need for a reliable, full‑service metal fabrication shop. The company remains family‑owned and is run day‑to‑day by the Rosses, with Rodney handling welding and field work while Brooke manages client relations and project coordination.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication including structural steel, pipe fencing, entryways, staircases, railings, decks, and bridges. Core processes cover MIG, TIG, and stick welding on carbon steel, stainless steel, and aluminum. Mid State Welding also operates mobile welding rigs that travel to job sites throughout the Black Hills, western South Dakota, and eastern Wyoming, offering on‑site equipment repair for farms, ranches, and commercial projects.

Customers include homeowners, general contractors, builders, and agricultural operators across the region. The firm regularly subcontracts on commercial construction projects and handles farm and ranch equipment repair and fence maintenance. Its certifications allow it to bid on state and federal contracts, and the team coordinates with an engineer to produce code‑compliant plans for decks and structural work.

The Rosses say they launched Mid State Welding to fill a gap for a trustworthy welding partner that could handle any project size while maintaining direct communication. Their stated values — professionalism, craftsmanship, trustworthiness, quality, and safety — guide every job, and they emphasize step‑by‑step visual updates so clients see progress from concept to completion.

The team set out to create a better solution for fecal incontinence after recognizing that existing products failed to adequately prevent leakage or restore patients' confidence.

The company develops, manufactures, and sells continence care products, most notably the StaySure® device—a discreet, silicone-based system designed to prevent accidental bowel leakage rather than merely contain or absorb it. Minnesota Medical Technologies designs and builds its own highly specialized, high-volume production systems, leveraging over 30 years of silicone expertise to control quality from concept through manufacturing.

The company serves the medical device and healthcare industries, focusing on fecal incontinence management. The team includes veterans of Rochester Medical Corporation, C.R. Bard, and Polaris Industries, bringing regulatory, quality, and commercial experience across Class I, II, and III medical devices.

Minnesota Medical Technologies was started because the founders believed current fecal incontinence products were not good enough—often failing to prevent leakage, control odor, or provide ease of use. Their mission is to deliver products of unmatched performance, comfort, and quality worldwide, restoring dignity and freedom to patients through innovative engineering and clinical insight.

Mitchell Furniture Systems traces its roots to Milwaukee, Wisconsin, where William Mitchell founded the company in 1896 to produce dairy-farm equipment such as automatic stalls, pens, and stanchions. Steel frames paired with wood tops remain the core construction method, and the company also offers a top-replacement service for both its own tables and competitors' units.

Primary customers are K–12 school districts, municipalities, churches, and commercial offices that need durable cafeteria, classroom, fellowship-hall, conference-room, and lecture-hall furniture. Mitchell's risers have served educational and municipal facilities since the late 1940s, and many early installations remain in service.

The company emphasizes "Made in America By Mitchell" as its differentiator, citing domestic production, robotic welding precision, and a design philosophy aimed at decades-long product life. Immediate delivery is advertised for stocked items.

about:
Mitsubishi Electric US, Inc., Industrial Automation operates from a facility in Vernon Hills, Illinois, serving as the Americas hub for the Japanese conglomerate's factory automation business. The parent company, Mitsubishi Electric Corporation, marked its 100th anniversary in February 2021, with the factory automation division representing a substantial portion of that legacy. The U.S. division was established to consolidate sales, marketing, service, engineering, and manufacturing resources under one roof.

The division designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of industrial automation equipment, including programmable logic controllers (MELSEC iQ-R, iQ-F, Q, L, and F series), human-machine interfaces (GOT3000 series), variable frequency drives (FREQROL FR-D800 series), AC servo systems (MELSERVO), industrial robots (MELFA), collaborative robots (ASSISTA), computerized numerical controllers, laser processing machines, and electrical discharge machines. The Vernon Hills campus integrates manufacturing, engineering, training, customer service, repair, sales, and warehousing functions, enabling end-to-end support for automation deployments.

Customers span mining, water and wastewater treatment, automotive, and education sectors. Documented projects include a comprehensive automation solution for mining safety and material handling with DICISA, a municipal lift station pump upgrade for energy efficiency with Bertelkamp Automation, robotic machine tending for e-motor production at Renault Group, and hands-on automation technology programs at Kettering University. The company also supports a network of Diamond Partner distributors, solutions providers, and OEMs, as well as system integrators through its Solutions Partner program.

The division's stated mission is to support the industrial automation needs of customers in the Americas through combined resources and a culture of continuous improvement (Kaizen). Mitsubishi Electric ranks among the top five global filers of international patent applications, and the company emphasizes product security through dedicated vulnerability management initiatives. Quality management systems underpin its commitment to meeting or exceeding customer expectations, while rapid repair turnaround using custom parts and on-site training aim to minimize downtime.

old_description: Sliver knitting, or high-pile knitting, is a process that locks individual fibers into a lightweight knit backing. The length of acrylic fibers used adds dimension and warmth to the fabric, when needed, without adding additional weight. Other advantages of using acrylic fibers include the incorporation of colorfast dyes and, a finished fabric that is odor and mildew resistant. The end result is a light, soft, comfortable fabric that is warmer than fleece and is machine washable and dryable.
about:
Monterey Mills operates from Janesville, Wisconsin. The company traces its current ownership to February 1995, when Dan Sinykin purchased the former Roller Fabrics after spending seven months working there without pay to evaluate the business. Sinykin, a former Procter & Gamble sales executive and founder of the Tailor’s Touch retail chain, assembled a management team, consolidated multiple plants, and expanded the product line into automotive, equestrian, apparel, hospital, and pet markets.

The mill specializes in sliver knitting — also called high-pile knitting — a labor‑intensive process that locks individual acrylic fibers into a lightweight knit backing. The technique yields fabrics that are warmer than fleece, odor‑ and mildew‑resistant, and machine washable. An in‑house R&D team controls fiber and yarn selection, pile height, density, tensile strength, width, color, and stitch count to develop performance fabrics for diverse applications. The company also produces blankets, bedding, and medical and pet products, all manufactured in the United States.

Customers span medical, pet, automotive, equestrian, apparel, and hospital sectors, as well as the blanket and bedding market. The firm’s technical capabilities allow it to tailor fabric specifications for OEMs and brand owners seeking custom performance textiles.

Monterey Mills positions itself as one of the few remaining U.S. practitioners of sliver knitting, a craft many competitors abandoned due to its complexity. The company emphasizes continuous improvement, domestic production, and sustainability — sourcing recycled raw materials, repurposing all production waste, and treating and reusing wastewater.

about:
Montrose Molders operates from Piscataway, New Jersey, where it was founded in 1966 by William Bruce Wilson. The company began as a 22-person tool shop producing tight-tolerance molds for the plastics industry. In 1972, the addition of its first injection molding press set the direction for future growth. Today, the business remains family-owned, led by the Wilson family, now in its fourth generation of plastics manufacturing.

The firm functions as a vertically integrated custom plastics manufacturer. Its facility houses 51 injection molding machines ranging from 40 to 1,000 tons of clamp force, two extrusion lines with co-extrusion capability, and an on-site tool and die shop that builds both aluminum and steel molds. A 25,000-square-foot assembly area runs up to five lines simultaneously, supporting decoration, assembly, and packaging. Engineering services include mold flow simulation via Solidworks Plastics and industrial design to translate concepts into 3D models.

Montrose serves a range of sectors including automotive, aerospace, medical devices, electronics, lighting, safety, battery, retail, and consumer goods. Customers engage the company for contract injection molding, extrusion, tooling, and full assembly programs, relying on its one-stop-shop model from design through finished product shipment.

The company emphasizes its family legacy and a culture of quality, consistency, and value. Each client is assigned a dedicated project manager to oversee complex projects from concept to delivery. Montrose highlights its ISO 9001:2015 certification and a focus on shortening lead times and reducing costs as core differentiators.

about:
Mountain Wire Rope Service is a family-owned business based in Selinsgrove, Pennsylvania. The company traces its roots to 1984 when Dale R. Walters, who had worked in the wire rope industry since 1968 at Paulsen Wire Rope Corp. in Sunbury, founded the firm. After Walters' death in October 2014, his daughter Whitney Walters-Anderson and her husband JT Anderson took over ownership; both had apprenticed under Dale and each brings more than 20 years of experience as a wire rope inspector and splicer.

The company specializes in aerial ropeway wire rope, offering splicing, repairs, inspections, magnetic rope testing, and sales of wire rope and lubricants. Operating from its central Pennsylvania location, the team travels worldwide to service wire rope from Maine to Jamaica. They inspect approximately 2 million feet of wire rope annually and, on a peak winter day, have 350 million people riding on lifts serviced by Mountain Wire Rope.

The primary customers are ski areas, amusement parks, and aerial tram operators. The firm currently services 135 ski areas and 10 amusement parks and aerial trams throughout the Caribbean, providing on-site inspection, splicing, and testing services.

Mountain Wire Rope Service distinguishes itself through its deep specialization in aerial ropeway applications and its ability to deploy inspection and splicing crews globally. The business was built on Dale Walters' decades of industry experience and continues as a family-led operation focused on wire rope safety and reliability.

name: Nashville Electric Service - Music City Solar
old_description: The city spoke. We listened. Thanks to the voice of our customers, what once was a landfill off I-65 is now the site of Nashville's first community solar park that includes 17,020 panels, available to participating customers, marking an important step in offering clean, efficient, maintenance-free energy.
about:
The initiative launched on August 1, 2018, when the utility transformed a former landfill off I-65 into Nashville's first community solar park. The project began after customers expressed demand for renewable energy options, prompting NES to develop a shared solar facility that would allow broad participation without rooftop installations.

The program manages a 17,020-panel solar array that feeds clean energy directly into the NES grid. Customers purchase subscriptions to individual panels and receive a monthly solar credit on their electric bills through 2038. As of the latest data, 3,142 panels are leased to customers, generating over 21 million kilowatt-hours to date. The park also reserves panels for the Solar Angel Fund, a donation-based component that provides energy assistance to low-income households; 1,015 panels have been donated so far, with 12,863 panels still available for new subscribers.

The service targets residential customers — both homeowners and renters — across the NES service territory who want renewable energy without upfront installation costs or maintenance. It also serves low-income households through the Solar Angel donation channel, administered in partnership with The Community Foundation of Middle Tennessee.

NES frames the program as a direct response to customer voice: "The city spoke. We listened." The utility emphasizes maintenance-free participation, long-term bill credits, and a community-focused model that combines environmental impact with local energy assistance. The park's location on a reclaimed landfill underscores a dual benefit of land reuse and emissions reduction.

name: National Molding
old_description: Global Manufacturer of Precision Engineered Plastic Components
about:
National Molding, headquartered in Miami Lakes, Florida, was founded in 1982. The company began as an injection molding specialist and developed proprietary Hetero Cavity technology that remains central to its operations today.

The company produces over 3.5 billion parts annually using highly engineered resins. Its capabilities span precision injection molding, medical product molding, metal-to-plastic conversions, low-cost modular molding, pre- and post-molding services, design for manufacturability, tooling design and manufacturing, cleanroom molding, insert over molding, and a full-service tool room with CNC machining. Molding machines range from 40 to 300 tons, supported by automation and assembly equipment. National Molding operates plants in the United States, Canada, and China, and over 80 percent of its output relies on the in-house Hetero Cavity process.

The medical division, certified to ISO 13485 and FDA registered, serves healthcare, life science, dental, and diagnostic markets from an ISO Class 8 cleanroom. Commercial lines cover plumbing fixtures, telecommunications, appliances, irrigation, furniture, marine, and electrical products. The DuraflexUSA division supplies Berry Amendment–compliant buckles and fasteners to sporting goods, military, tactical, and pet-supply markets, while a separate line produces tactical body armor release systems for military and law enforcement.

National Molding differentiates itself through its proprietary Hetero Cavity injection molding technology, developed internally and used across the majority of its parts. The company also offers full consulting and rapid-response contract engineering services, and maintains ISO 9001, ISO 13485, and IATF 16949 certifications across its operations.

New Berlin Plastics was founded in 1975 by William Aukofer and Robert Zeman in New Berlin, Wisconsin. After relocations in 1976 and 1982, the company moved into a 100,000-square-foot facility in 1998 that serves as its corporate headquarters and manufacturing site. In July 2001, Jeffery Held and Mark Siewert acquired the business and have since directed its growth.

The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding, with a focus on scientific injection molding, medical device components, engineered plastic parts, and precision molded products for OEMs across Wisconsin and North America. Operations run from the 100,000-square-foot plant, supplemented by a recently acquired second building to meet rising demand. The firm emphasizes automation, mold flow analysis, and design-for-manufacturability support, and manages over 100 simultaneous customer projects through its proprietary LaunchLogic program.

New Berlin Plastics serves a diverse set of industries, including electrical utility, automotive and transportation, specialty hand and power tools, power sports, water treatment, building and construction, controls, healthcare and medical devices, lawn and garden, industrial, pet care, marine, and small engine. Customers are primarily OEMs that value high-quality engineered components and supply-chain reliability.

The company differentiates itself through tightly controlled scientific molding processes, a 99.8% customer acceptance rate, a 2.2% internal scrap rate, and a 98% on-time launch track record via LaunchLogic. Automation integration and comprehensive value-added services — from resin selection to tool transfer — are cited as core strengths.

about:
North Dakota Soybean Processors (NDSP) operates a soybean crushing facility in Casselton, North Dakota. The company was formed as a joint venture between CGB Enterprises, Inc., a private U.S. grain and transportation company with a 50-year history, and Minnesota Soybean Processors (MnSP). CGB Enterprises, through its subsidiary Consolidated Grain and Barge Co., operates a network of over 100 grain facilities across the Midwest and has run a soy-crushing plant in Mt. Vernon, Indiana, with a daily capacity exceeding 140,000 bushels since 1997. NDSP extends that processing footprint into the Red River Valley, giving local growers a year-round market for their soybeans.

The Casselton plant produces food-grade soybean oil, soybean meal, and soyhull pellets. The facility is described as state-of-the-art, designed to crush soybeans sourced from North Dakota and surrounding areas. NDSP offers producers a blended portfolio of pricing tools to manage risk and capture value.

NDSP serves the food, renewable fuel, and livestock feed industries. Its food-grade oil targets food manufacturers and the growing renewable diesel sector, while its meal supplies livestock producers. The company’s customer base includes soybean farmers in Cass County and the broader Red River Valley who deliver grain directly to the plant. Testimonials from state officials, county commissioners, and local farmers highlight the facility’s role in adding value to the regional agricultural economy.

NDSP states its mission is to sustainably produce and deliver high-quality soybean products for food and fuel markets while fostering a safe, supportive environment for employees, customers, and the community. Leadership emphasizes that local processing creates jobs, stimulates the economy, and provides farmers with more profitable harvest options. The venture was started to capture value from North Dakota soybeans within the state rather than shipping raw beans elsewhere.

The company runs a dedicated structural steel fabrication plant in Fayette, Alabama, and manages a network of ten North American facilities stretching from Monterrey, Mexico, to Cedar Falls, Iowa.

OMS specializes in heavy steel fabrication, precision welding, complex CNC machining, and 5-axis laser processing, supported by advanced automation such as a robotic beam line, plasma and saw cutting, and paint finishing. The facilities produce high-volume repetitive parts, heavy-duty welded assemblies, and fabricated metal components for OEM supply chains, offering kitting and assembly as value-added services.

The company serves global OEMs in power generation, data centers, construction, material handling, transportation, and renewable energy. Its customer base includes Tier 1 partners in heavy equipment and infrastructure markets who rely on multi-site production for supply chain stability.

OMS differentiates itself through integrated multi-site manufacturing, providing a single point of contact for multi-step metal processing across its North American network. The company emphasizes proactive risk management, technical repeatability, and structural integrity, leveraging a century of industrial expertise to ensure on-time delivery and quality at scale.

about:
OMG Tooling Inc was founded in 1980 by Oliver Marino Gerardi in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. Gerardi, known as the "original OMG," began by leasing a small space and operating a tool and die shop, sketching initial concepts on napkins before translating them into tooling and molds. His blend of art and science, combined with a passion for quality, established the company's foundation.

The company provides full-service plastic injection molding, encompassing custom design, in-house tooling fabrication, and molding of plastic components. OMG maintains tooling capabilities that many molders have eliminated, allowing it to build advanced tooling, enhance existing molds, and manage transfer tooling from other suppliers. Its automated molding processes aim to deliver consistent quality at competitive production rates, positioning the firm as a domestic alternative to overseas sourcing.

OMG serves original equipment manufacturers across a range of sectors, including consumer goods, healthcare, sports and leisure, construction, transportation, infrastructure, electronics, technology, and industrial markets. The company highlights its ability to accept existing molds as transfer tooling, supporting customers who need to relocate production or extend tool life.

The firm emphasizes its U.S.-based manufacturing and central Oklahoma location as strategic supply-chain advantages, promoting "Made in USA" integrity and protection against intellectual property risks associated with global supply chains. Core values articulated by the founder—integrity, excellence, quality, dedication, loyalty, and customer service—are cited as the bedrock of its operations.

old_description: OTHER Industries is a studio specializing in custom screen printing, embroidery, promo products and bulk wholesale apparel production located in Wilmington, Delaware. With over 10 years of experience, we produce high quality custom printed t-shirts, branded merchandise, and large scale production runs with fast, reliable turnaround times. about:
OTHER Industries operates from Wilmington, Delaware, where it began over a decade ago as a basement operation printing shirts for the founders' own clothing projects. The studio grew from those DIY roots into a full‑service apparel production facility, shaped by the graphic‑design and printmaking communities of nearby Philadelphia.

The company provides custom screen printing, embroidery, promotional‑product sourcing, and wholesale apparel manufacturing. All production is kept in‑house at the Wilmington location, where experienced printers handle artwork review, screen setup, printing, and quality control. The shop works with plastisol, water‑based, and discharge inks, offers Pantone color matching, and runs specialty inks such as puff, glow‑in‑the‑dark, metallic, reflective, glitter, suede, plush, high‑density, texture, and stretch formulations. Orders start at 24 pieces for screen printing and scale from small‑batch runs to large wholesale volumes.

Clients span clothing brands, restaurants and coffee shops, construction and trade firms, schools and universities, corporate organizations, artists and bands, festivals and live‑event producers, nonprofits, breweries and hospitality groups, and retail merchandise programs. The studio decorates a wide range of garments including T‑shirts, hoodies, long‑sleeve shirts, tanks, athletic and performance wear, work shirts, safety apparel, polos, tote bags, aprons, jackets, sweatpants, and shorts.

The founders chose the name OTHER Industries to signal a departure from traditional print shops, aiming for a studio more connected to design, music, and independent brand culture. Their approach balances design awareness, technical experience, and hands‑on craftsmanship, with a dedicated sales representative guiding each order from garment selection through finished delivery.

name: OVERTAKE
old_description: In 2019, Justin Grimm sold his previous company to a private equity firm. Very soon after, he realized that the original values of the company started to slip away. He also realized this was not only happening with his own company, it was unfortunately becoming a frequent thing in the aftermarket community. He saw the soul of the automotive scene slipping away. The smaller shops, the craftsmanship, the community-focused values — all were being overshadowed by corporate giants more interested in profits than passion. So, he took a step back, reimagined the future, and founded OVERTAKE to give enthusiasts, like you, the parts, service, and attention to detail that you deserve.
about:
OVERTAKE is based in St. Paul, Minnesota, and was founded in 2019 by Justin Grimm. After selling his previous automotive business to a private equity firm, Grimm observed that the original values of craftsmanship and community focus were eroding across the aftermarket sector. He established OVERTAKE to restore enthusiast-driven service and attention to detail for the Subaru community.

The company designs and manufactures performance parts for Subaru vehicles spanning WRX, STI, BRZ/86, Forester, Crosstrek, Impreza, Outback, Legacy, and Ascent models. Product lines include top-mount intercoolers, gasket sets for H6 engines, transmission mount inserts, post-MAF pipe kits, cam solenoid heat shields, and various accessories. Operations emphasize crowd-sourced development through a dedicated Facebook group where enthusiasts provide feedback before production.

The company supports contingency racing sponsorships and influencer partnerships, and maintains a dealer network for wholesale distribution. Hero discounts are offered to military personnel, teachers, and healthcare workers.

The founder states the business was started to counter a trend where corporate ownership prioritizes profit over passion. Differentiators include same-day shipping on orders placed by 2 p.m. CST, a 30-day return policy, free shipping on orders over $250 within the lower 48 states, and a pricing philosophy that aims to keep custom-engineered products accessible.

name: Oberlin Filter Company
old_description: The best pressure filter company depends on the specific filtration requirements, industrial application, and performance needs. Oberlin Filter is a leading provider of high-quality filtration solutions that effectively remove up to 99.99% of suspended solids from liquids.
about:
Oberlin Filter Company is based in Pewaukee, Wisconsin. The company states it has over 60 years of proven experience in pressure filtration, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details and founder names are not provided in the available information.

The company designs and manufactures pressure filtration systems that remove up to 99.99% of suspended solids from liquids down to 1 micron. Its product line includes the OLIMIN8R™ for single CNC machine coolant filtration, the Oberlin Hot Oil Filter for food‑processing frying and roasting operations, and a range of automatic pressure filters that operate at up to 40 PSI differential pressure. The filtration process forces contaminated fluid through filter media, traps particles, and automatically discharges a dry filter cake, eliminating wet sludge handling. The company reports serving more than 380 manufacturers, from Fortune 500 global operations to local machine shops.

Oberlin filters are used across a broad set of industries: industrial coolant systems (oil, water‑soluble emulsions, synthetics), metal finishing (phosphate bath recycling), food processing (frying and roasting oil), sulfur recovery, CNC machining, maritime scrubber systems, breweries and sludge dewatering, chemical processing, semiconductor and solar wastewater (silicon fines, gallium arsenide, heavy metals), crystallizer zero‑liquid‑discharge (ZLD) applications, and general industrial process wastewater treatment.

The company emphasizes that its differentiation lies in the dry‑cake discharge — turning waste into a handleable solid — which automates compliance, maximizes fluid recovery, and removes manual labor. It also highlights 40 PSI pressure force (four times gravity filtration), a typical 6‑ to 12‑month payback, and up to 80% reduction in filter media costs compared with alternative systems.

name: Occam Design
old_description: Welcome to Occam Design. Meeting your specs, exceeding your expectations.
about:
Occam Design, based in Louisville, Kentucky, was founded in 2006 as a division of CreoSalus, Inc. The company operates from two facilities in Louisville, including a main office on East Oak Street and a manufacturing facility on East Chestnut Street.

The firm provides end-to-end medical device development and cGMP manufacturing, covering project management, design for manufacturing, test development, production prototyping, regulatory compliance, and wellness/wearables device development. Its Louisville facilities house five Class 7 cleanrooms, a machine shop, and injection molding equipment, all within an FDA-registered, ISO 13485:2016-certified environment.

Occam serves clients across the U.S. and Europe, including medical device companies developing Class I, II, and III products, health-tech and wearables startups, equine device developers, and government-funded projects (NIH, DOD). Past clients include DeltaChase LLC, Trio Medical, Cerovations, MagnaWave, and a Fortune 1000 company, as well as universities such as Yale, Harvard, Duke, and the University of Louisville.

The company’s approach is guided by Occam’s Razor—“entities should not be multiplied unnecessarily”—emphasizing lean operations and a dedicated project manager who coordinates engineering, regulatory, and manufacturing resources. Occam highlights its ability to start or stop work dynamically, identify development and regulatory gaps, and maintain compliance with IEC 60601 and CISPR-11 standards for electro-medical equipment.

Based in Norman, Oklahoma, Off Grid Enterprises, LLC provides turnkey renewable-energy installations. The company's project manager, Pieter Huebner, is a NABCEP-certified installer with 30 years in the field, including 1984–2013 as lead installer and trainer at Bergey Wind Power where he designed off-grid power systems worldwide.

The company designs, builds, and installs off-grid and grid-tied solar and wind systems for residential, commercial, agricultural, and remote sites. Installations include ground-mounted, roof-mounted, pergola, and carport arrays, as well as battery backup and generator-integrated systems. References span from Belize to Alaska, including a 10 kW Bergey wind turbine at a remote Alaskan site.

Customers include homeowners, businesses, farms, and remote facilities seeking energy independence or grid-tied savings. Projects cited range from a residential ranch installation to a 10 kW Bergey wind system at a remote Alaskan site, as well as installations in Belize, Canada, Maine, and across the continental U.S.

Off Grid Enterprises stresses that every installation is overseen by a NABCEP-certified professional, ensuring code compliance and system reliability. The firm highlights its use of U.S.-manufactured equipment, comprehensive warranties, and free site surveys to help customers capture federal tax credits and long-term utility savings.

about:
Ogonek Custom Hardwoods operates from Barberton, Ohio, in the heart of Northeast Ohio. While the exact founding year isn’t public, the company describes its origins as rooted in a family’s love for a place that represents more than an investment.

The sawmill cuts beams and timbers up to 52 feet long in species native to the area, including white pine, red oak, aspen, white oak, cherry, and black walnut. Beyond rough-sawn and planed timbers, the shop produces tongue-and-groove decking, specialty blocking and dunnage, live-edge slabs, and hand-hewn beams. about:
Ohio Metal Fabricating Inc. operates from Dayton, Ohio, where it has built over forty years of experience in metal spinning and fabrication.

The shop specializes in hand metal spinning and CNC metal spinning, complemented by flat and three‑dimensional laser cutting. It can spin parts up to 104 inches in diameter with material thicknesses from 0.010 to 0.187 inches, holding tolerances as tight as 0.002 inches. In‑house capabilities extend to welding, penetrant inspection, punching, beading, anodizing, plating, painting, polishing, and custom assembly. Ninety‑nine percent of spinning tools and dies are produced internally, and CNC cells handle secondary operations such as trimming and drilling. Equipment includes six‑axis laser systems and an M & M CNC lathe with flanging and cutting functions.

The company serves customers across multiple industries, collaborating directly with their engineering and quality teams to reduce costs and shorten lead times. Its one‑stop‑shop model targets complex spun or laser‑cut metal components for clients who need integrated finishing and inspection services.

Ohio Metal Fabricating emphasizes an on‑time delivery rate above 99 percent, competitive pricing, and short lead times. The business was built on the premise that combining quality, speed, and precision benefits the customer’s bottom line, and it continues to position itself as a cost‑advantaged alternative to other fabrication methods.

about:
Oklahoma Shirt Company operates as a screen printing and apparel shop in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. Founded by a team passionate about design, craftsmanship, and Oklahoma culture, the company has grown into a partner for businesses, schools, organizations, and events across the state.

The shop provides custom screen printing, embroidery, promotional products, signage, stickers, graphic design, direct-to-film printing, and online gear store services. Its capabilities include SIM process separations for screen printing and a subscription-based Shirt of the Month program. Minimum orders start at 24 garments per design for screen printing, with direct-to-film and embroidery available at five-piece minimums.

Customers range from local businesses and schools to statewide organizations and events. A notable client is the Oklahoma City Thunder, for which the company serves as the official printing partner.

The company states that its purpose extends beyond brand promotion, aiming to build connection, celebrate community, and tell stories through apparel. It emphasizes thoughtful design, quality materials, and modern production to deliver products that stand out.
